for: The presentation: the pier study (deck slides 7 and 8) as one drawing. Not placed in the deck yet.
shows: The same pier, R1.P1, with the same four climbers, grown twice by the plant simulator and shown side by side for ten years, straight on from outside the room at one scale: on the left its legs stand together, on the right they stand apart, as the design has them. Only time moves, slowly, and both sides in step; it holds on June of the tenth year and loops. Over each picture, how many of its four climbers get the light they ask for and how high they have reached. Below, the six openings studied, in plan, with their climbers in the right light and the way in; those the footing draft rejects are struck, the design ringed. Drag the rail to move through the years.
statement: Every stem, leaf and flower is the plant simulator's: two runs, one seed each, the same planting on two versions of the building, on this study's designed site; species numbers are provisional assumptions. Leaves and flowers are plain marks. The strip's figures are the simulator's reading of each species' light against its own provisional profile, the building model's way in, and this study's ground draft for the footing, which is not engineering. Across the room the two runs end with about the same total length of stem; what differs is light, height and flower. A scenario, not a forecast.
